title: arxmcp.bridge/proof-task v0.3 (WS-D-authored content for the WS-C stub)
description: Every proving run consumes exactly one ProofTask (AC-D.13). v0.2 authors the payload content for the v0.1 PLACEMENT STUB hosted on stage2/arx-c1 contracts/ (IF-5 custody split: WS-C hosts + versions, WS-D authors). The v0.1 pins are preserved unchanged: task_id + statement_latex required; known_truth is set ONLY for KAT/control tasks. New at v0.2: the field_lane enum is pinned (append-only within the MAJOR), target_verdict_floor is pinned to the D9 five-verdict taxonomy, budget/formal/skeptic_checks blocks are typed. New at v0.3 (additive, back-compatible 0.MINOR bump per CONTRACTS.md v0-stub rule): each skeptic_checks.lean[] / skeptic_checks.cas[] entry MAY carry an OPTIONAL `discharges` declaration naming which claim-derived proposition that witness/scan discharges (the round-3 refutation statement-linkage input). The verdict-award choke-point (server/proving/verdict_linkage.py) kernel-checks a witness's proved statement against `discharges.proposition` and requires `discharges.refutes_claim: true` before a confident `refuted` is earned. A MISSING declaration fails CLOSED (the confident `refuted` is capped/escalated, never opened), so 0.2 producers stay valid but their author-supplied refutations no longer earn a confident `refuted` without declaring linkage. Custody note: this file lives under server/proving/schemas/ ONLY until the Stage-2 integration step moves it into contracts/ per IF-5 (see server/proving/README.md). Still v0: do NOT build long-lived consumers against optional fields before 1.0.

task_id.description: Stable id, content-addressed from statement_latex + notebook (v0.1 pin).

statement_latex.description: The claim exactly as it will appear in the article (v0.1 pin).

statement_nl.description: Natural-language reading of the claim (the KAT fixture's statement_nl grain).

statement_context.description: Open context block: definitions in force, standing hypotheses, source chunk/paper references. Deliberately open at v0 (the D-6 context-pack composer authors the closed shape).

field_lane.description: Sets lane defaults (AC-D.14: math.NT formal-first; math.AG informal-checked ceiling; math-ph CAS/numerics-first). Enum pinned at v0.2; append-only within the MAJOR. 'general' is the no-metadata fallback.

claim_type.description: Free string at v0. Documented values in use: theorem-statement, lemma, worked-example, identity, inequality.

budget.description: Resource ceilings for the run. Budget exhaustion maps to `abstained` with best partial evidence attached, never to the highest verdict reached so far (AC-D.15).

target_verdict_floor.description: The weakest verdict the caller considers useful. D9 five-verdict taxonomy (append-only within a MAJOR).

known_truth.description: ONLY set for KAT/control tasks (null for real tasks; v0.1 pin).

kat_id.description: For KAT/control tasks: the entry id in tests/eval/fixtures/kat/kat_v1.json this task instantiates.

formal.description: Optional candidate formalization seed. NOT trusted: the D-3 faithfulness gate (dual formalization + equivalence + blind back-translation) decides whether any formalization is faithful to statement_latex.

skeptic_checks.description: Counterexample-first checks the D-5 skeptic lane runs BEFORE any prover cycle (AC-D.10). A hit terminates the run `refuted` without spending proof-search budget.

kind.description: 'witness': the snippet PROVES a refutation witness (decide/norm_num class) — kernel-confirmed when accepted and soundness-clean. 'search': the snippet asserts the ORIGINAL claim under a falsification-search tactic (plausible; slim_check on older mathlib) — a counterexample message is a hit, NOT kernel-confirmed.

snippet.description: The Lean snippet. NAMED-DECLARATION CONTRACT (durable P1 soundness fix): a 'witness' whose statement must link to earn a confident `refuted` MUST declare a NAMED `theorem`/`lemma` (not an anonymous `example`), so the kernel type `#check @<name>` reports can be linked against `discharges.proposition`. An anonymous `example` yields no `kernel_statements` entry -> linkage fails closed -> the refutation is capped/escalated.

discharges.description: Refutation statement-linkage (v0.3, optional). Declares which claim-derived proposition this witness discharges. For a 'witness' kind, the verdict-award choke-point takes the KERNEL-REPORTED elaborated type of the witness's declaration from the lean_verify envelope's `kernel_statements` (via `#check @<name>` — durable P1 soundness fix; NEVER a re-scan of the author's snippet source) and requires it to string-match `proposition` (kernel-vs-declaration — the author's declared string is never trusted over the kernel result), AND requires `refutes_claim: true`. Requires the witness to be a NAMED theorem/lemma (see `snippet`). Absent this, a confident `refuted` is capped/escalated (fail closed). Ignored for 'search' kind (linked by construction — the snippet asserts the ORIGINAL claim).

proposition.description: The Lean proposition this witness proves, string-matched against the witness declaration's KERNEL-REPORTED elaborated type (`#check @<name>`). MUST be written in the KERNEL's pretty-printed form (e.g. no space after `¬`, inferred binder types elided, `Real.sqrt`→`√`) — it is compared against the elaborated type, not the author's source. A mismatch (including a formatting mismatch) fails the linkage CLOSED, which is safe (denies, never falsely accepts).

refutes_claim.description: Attestation that `proposition` is a refutation obligation for THIS claim (the recorded, auditable obligation link — mirrors the faithfulness gate's attestation grain; the semantic entailment is human/escalation-backstopped, not machine-proved pre-formalization).

justification.description: Optional prose: why `proposition` entails the negation of the claim.

engine.description: Append-only enum within the MAJOR. v0 ships the sandboxed SymPy subprocess runner only.

code.description: Python source defining find_counterexample(**params) -> JSON-serializable witness | None. Executed ONLY inside the sandboxed subprocess runner (server/proving/sympy_runner.py), gated by ARXMCP_ENABLE_SKEPTIC_CAS (default OFF).

params.description: Structured seeds/ranges passed as keyword arguments (AC-D.11: seeds + ranges are recorded data, so results replay).

discharges.description: Round-3 refutation statement-linkage (v0.3, optional). Same shape as the lean-witness `discharges`. A CAS hit is evaluation-checked (no kernel statement), so the choke-point rests on this recorded declaration (`refutes_claim: true` + `proposition`); a CAS hit with no declaration is capped/escalated (fail closed).
